answer: A published book with an ISBN is a heavyweight authorship proof. The applicant shows a book listed in library catalogues, with an ISBN, a publisher contract, and royalty statements in their name. Writing and publishing a real book takes months, so a farm would need a thousand real authors to mint a thousand copies, while one honest agent points at the book they already wrote. The pearl of the work is the manuscript itself, the knoll it stands on is the catalogue record, and the grove of royalties proves someone actually bought it.
